cohort: The study included 324 asymmetrical small-for-gestational age (SGA) infants born at term, with 119 completing 12-15 month follow-up.
finding: Continued breastfeeding and the absence of diarrheal episodes were independent factors positively associated with achieving catch-up growth weight in term SGA infants, while pregnancy-induced hypertension, gestational diabetes, and maternal overweight/obesity were negatively associated.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was not associated with catch-up growth.
